rendering.persona_description: Asher is a 68-year-old retired postal carrier who spent thirty-two years sorting and delivering mail before his knees gave out. He transitioned in his forties and has been with his wife, Doreen, for twenty-six years; they have a grown son from her first marriage whom Asher helped raise. He keeps a vegetable garden and volunteers twice a month at the local VFW hall doing paperwork. He is a precise, orderly man who takes pride in never having lost anything important, or so he says.
rendering.clinical_context: Asher has obsessive-compulsive disorder centered on doubt and checking: he is plagued by the fear that he has left the stove on, failed to lock the door, or, when driving, struck something without noticing, and he cannot rest until he has verified this to his own satisfaction, which often he cannot. The checking began in his fifties after a small kitchen fire at a previous house, though it has since spread well beyond stoves to locks, appliances, and his car. He tried a course of exposure and response prevention with a psychologist some years back but stopped attending, finding the exercises unbearable, and he is not in any treatment now.
rendering.behavioral_description: Asher is polite and cooperative, and tends to agree with what a professional tells him even when he does not believe it changes anything for him personally. He describes his checking rituals in careful, circumstantial detail, as if giving testimony, and treats the danger of fire or a hit-and-run as simply factual rather than as a symptom. He will say he understands why the checking is not helping and then, in the same breath, explain why this particular time it really was necessary. He rarely pushes back directly; he nods along and quietly keeps doing what he was already doing.

traits.living_situation: lives with his wife in a house they own
traits.communication_register: plain, orderly, and detail-oriented; describes routines like giving a report
traits.help_seeking_orientation: was compliant with providers when he was in treatment, agreeing readily but struggling to carry out what was asked; not currently seeking or engaged in any treatment
traits.cognitive_style: concrete, methodical, prone to circumstantial detail and repeated self-justification of checking

clinical_history.presentation: obsessive-compulsive disorder, doubt and checking theme
clinical_history.history: checking behaviors began in his fifties after a small kitchen fire and have gradually spread from the stove to locks, appliances, and driving over the past fifteen years; he began a course of exposure and response prevention some years ago but discontinued it, and it has been more than a year since he was last in any treatment.

symptoms: repeated checking of stove, locks, and appliances
returning to re-check while driving, for fear of having hit something unnoticed
intrusive doubt that a check was done thoroughly enough
significant time spent on checking rituals
distress and difficulty resisting the urge to check even briefly
